concurrency_and_state: Input.PLAYER_ID_OBJECT is a non-thread-safe HashMap<Integer, Object> accessed concurrently by Netty worker threads in createFormChangeName/createFormUseCardQuantity/doInput, and player.idMark.getTypeInput() is never cleared after Input.doInput executes, allowing packet replay.

Input.java TANG_THOI_VANG, TANG_NGOC_XANH, TANG_NGOC_HONG, BANSLL, and USE_CARD_QUANTITY mutate player inventory/currency without synchronizing on player (or target player), and offline gifts race with concurrent player login.

Trade.java uses deterministic lock ordering on player.getTradeLock() (by ascending player.id) during startTrade() and synchronized methods on Trade instance, but snapshots itemsBag1/itemsBag2 at constructor time and overwrites player.inventory.itemsBag on commit without locking or invalidating concurrent inventory mutations (e.g., Input.BANSLL, Input.TANG_NGOC_HONG, Input.USE_CARD_QUANTITY).
TransactionService maintains a static ConcurrentHashMap<Player, Trade> PLAYER_TRADE and runs a background daemon loop (sleep 50-300ms) calling trade.update() for 180s timeout cancellation.
LuckyRound acquires nested synchronized(player) -> synchronized(player.inventory.itemsBoxCrackBall) cleanly for gem and ticket spins.

CSMM uses ConcurrentHashMap<Player, List<Integer>> with CopyOnWriteArrayList keyed by Player object reference; HandleCSMM and Register are synchronized on CSMM, holding the lock across ServerNotify and network sends while also failing to reward players who reconnected with a new Player instance.

SummonDragon and SummonDragonNamek store global singleton summon state (playerSummonShenron, isShenronAppear, menuShenron, select) updated by unsynchronized background threads and Netty threads; SummonDragon.pl_dragonStar is a raw HashMap<Player, Byte> that never removes entries.

UseItem.getItem synchronizes on player, whereas UseItem.doItem, UseItem.useItem, ChestBoxItemHandler, ConsumableItemHandler, and SpecialItemHandler do not synchronize on player when checking and consuming bag items.
ItemActionManager uses a plain ArrayList<ItemActionHandler> populated in a synchronized singleton constructor, with registerHandler exposed publicly without synchronization.
cross_module_questions: Confirm on the Unity Client and Message/NpcMenuController side how opcode -83 is parsed for DRAGON_PORUNGA vs DRAGON_SHENRON (SummonDragonNamek omits int playerId that SummonDragon writes).
Verify whether NpcFactory/Controller clears player.idMark.setTypeInput(-1) elsewhere or if -125 can be replayed directly from the client.
Check PlayerDAO.updatePlayer and NDVSqlFetcher.loadPlayerByName / loadById concurrency behavior when Input or SummonDragonNamek modifies offline players while login is in flight.
Check how ShopService.getRubyPrice vs ShopService.COST_GEM differ in MuaCtService so cosmetic inspection purchase pricing and commission currency are consistent.
Verify NpcMenuController handling of ConstNpc.CONFIRM_CHANGE_PET to confirm whether player.isConfirmingChangePet / player.itemToConfirmChangePet are reset outside SpecialItemHandler.changePet.

findings.impact: Players can duplicate items by trading with themselves, or by mutating their real bag (via Input.BANSLL, Input.USE_CARD_QUANTITY, etc.) while Trade is open and having Trade overwrite inventory.itemsBag on commit.
findings.root_cause: 1) TransactionService allows SEND_INVITE_TRADE/ACCEPT_TRADE when playerId == pl.id (creating new Trade(pl, pl)), where itemsBag2 gets itemsTrade1 added and overwrites player.inventory.itemsBag. 2) Trade snapshots itemsBag1/itemsBag2 at constructor time and overwrites real inventory on commit, while Input cases BANSLL/TANG_NGOC_HONG/USE_CARD_QUANTITY do not check isTrade/TransactionService.check.
findings.title: Self-Trade & Snapshot-Overwrite Item Duplication in Trade/TransactionService

findings.impact: Any client with typeInput set (or via replay) can trigger admin VND buff, item creation, bot spawning, global notice, or player rename without admin privilege checks; additionally, replayable typeInput enables concurrent race/double-spend in TANG_NGOC_HONG and BANSLL.
findings.root_cause: Input.BUFFVND, GIVE_IT, DUNGLOA, BOTQUAI*, BOTBOSS, and CHANGE_NAME lack if (!player.isAdmin()) checks (unlike SEND_ITEM_OP and GET_IT). Input.doInput never resets player.idMark.setTypeInput(-1) and lacks synchronized(player), and TANG_NGOC_HONG lacks trade checks and locks.
findings.title: Missing Admin Checks, Unreset typeInput, and Unsynchronized Economy Cases in Input.java

findings.impact: Guaranteed binary stream desync / EOFException / crash on all online clients when Namek Shenron (Porunga) is summoned or dismissed.
findings.root_cause: SummonDragonNamek.activeShenron writes opcode -83 with mapId, bgId, zoneId, then UTF(pl.name) — omitting the 4-byte int(pl.id) that SummonDragon.activeShenron writes before UTF. Also neither activeShenron cleans up Message(-83) in a finally block, leaking Netty buffers.
findings.title: Opcode -83 Stream Desync and Message Leak in SummonDragonNamek & SummonDragon

findings.impact: Players can summon 1-star/2-star/3-star Shenron without consuming the primary dragon ball, summon black/normal dragon concurrently or crash background timer into permanent server-wide Shenron lockout, and fallthrough grants two pet skill rerolls.
findings.root_cause: checkShenronBall(pl) never verifies the initiating 1/2/3-star ball is still in bag and summonShenron silently swallows NPE in try/catch when subQuantityItemsBag receives null. SHEN_RON_BI_NGO case 0 lacks break and falls into case 1. shenronLeave calls NpcService on potentially null/offline playerSummonShenron from the unsynchronized timer thread, leaving isShenronAppear=true if NPE occurs.
findings.title: Free Shenron Summon Exploit, Case Fallthrough, and Lockout NPE in SummonDragon

findings.impact: Players can open Wood Chest (570) infinitely without waiting for midnight, lose items when bag is full, or crash on out-of-bounds param; players can craft Dragon Egg (1426) from 1 shard instead of 99.
findings.root_cause: openWoodChest never updates pl.lastTimeRewardWoodChest = System.currentTimeMillis() and never checks getCountEmptyBag or itemOptions bounds. open1427 calls subQuantityItemsBag(pl, item, 99) without verifying item.quantity >= 99.
findings.title: Infinite Wood Chest Exploit & 1-for-99 Item Craft Exploit in ChestBoxItemHandler

findings.impact: Players can keep or reuse the pet-change item (401) across confirmations or leave isConfirmingChangePet permanently true after changing pet.
findings.root_cause: changePet stores player.itemToConfirmChangePet and sets player.isConfirmingChangePet = true, but on confirmation never checks if itemToConfirmChangePet is still in itemsBag with quantity >= 1 and never resets isConfirmingChangePet = false or itemToConfirmChangePet = null.
findings.title: Unvalidated & Unreset Pet-Change State Exploit in SpecialItemHandler.changePet

findings.impact: Exhausts HikariCP database connection pool under player rename attempts.
findings.root_cause: AlyraManager.executeQuery("select * from player where name = ?", text[0]).next() discards the returned AlyraResultSet without closing/disposing it.
findings.title: Unclosed AlyraResultSet Connection Leak in Input.CHANGE_NAME & CHANGE_NAME_BY_ITEM

findings.impact: Trade lock packet (-86 sub 6) causes stream desync when two trading players use client versions across the 222 threshold; Maintenance during LOCK_TRADE/ACCEPT causes NPE when trade is null.
findings.root_cause: Trade.lockTran checks sender's session.version < 222 instead of receiver's session.version < 222 before sending quantity as byte vs int. TransactionService checks Maintenance.isRunning and calls trade.cancelTrade() before null-checking trade.
findings.title: Trade Lock Version Check Mismatch & NullPointerException on Maintenance

findings.impact: Players who disconnect and reconnect before the 5-minute CSMM draw lose their ruby payout; concurrent login/disconnect loses rewards.
findings.root_cause: listRegNumber keys on Player object identity instead of playerId; HandleCSMM verifies online status via Client.gI().getPlayer(pl.id) != null, then credits plWins containing the stale disconnected Player reference.
findings.title: Stale Player Reference Keying Loses Winnings on Reconnect in CSMM

findings.impact: Players with a stack of Xinbato Water Bottles (456) lose up to 99 bottles on a single use; Radar cards with Max/maxLevel > 127 overflow byte maxPerLevel and grant max level for 0 cards.
findings.root_cause: useBinhNuocXinbato checks item.quantity >= 1 then subtracts 99. useCardBatch casts maxPerLevel and card.Amount to signed byte (overflowing > 127 to negative).
findings.title: Wrong Item Deduction (99 vs 1) in ConsumableItemHandler & Byte Overflow in SpecialItemHandler.useCardBatch

findings.impact: Race conditions between UseItem.doItem/useItem and UseItem.getItem/Trade/throwItem allow double-use or IndexOutOfBoundsException crashes.
findings.root_cause: UseItem.doItem and useItem do not synchronize on player (unlike getItem), DO_THROW_ITEM lacks upper bounds checks on itemsBody/itemsBag index, and index == -1 passes -1 to MountPetItemHandler.handle -> itemBagToBody(player, -1).
findings.title: Unsynchronized UseItem.doItem & Missing Index Bounds Checks

findings.impact: Namek dragon wish stalls Netty thread with up to ~50 blocking DB roundtrips and risks ConcurrentModificationException and offline login overwrite races; MuaCtService mismatches ruby/gem pricing and credits offline/unlocked sellers.
findings.root_cause: SummonDragonNamek iterates clan.members synchronously calling NDVSqlFetcher.loadById and PlayerDAO.updatePlayer per offline member. MuaCtService previews price with getRubyPrice() but charges/matches COST_GEM and credits seller.inventory.gem without verifying online status or locking seller/buyer.
findings.title: Blocking N+1 DB Loop in SummonDragonNamek & Price/Lock Mismatch in MuaCtService

findings.impact: Memory leak of Player/Item objects, potential ConcurrentModificationException or HashMap corruption, and Message ByteBuf leak on exception in SkillBookItemHandler.
findings.root_cause: Input.PLAYER_ID_OBJECT and SummonDragon.pl_dragonStar use raw/unsynchronized HashMap and leak entries when players cancel forms or summon menus; SkillBookItemHandler.learnSkill does not place msg.cleanup() in finally.
findings.title: Unsynchronized HashMap Leaks & Missing Message Cleanup in SkillBookItemHandler

module_summary: Covers player-facing economy, trading, minigame, dragon summoning, dialog input, and item-use subsystems under services.func and services.func.useitem. Item usage was refactored into a Strategy/Facade architecture (UseItem -> ItemActionManager -> 7 handlers), while Trade uses ordered ReentrantLocks on snapshotted bags. Major P0/P1 risks center on missing privilege/trade/quantity/state checks in Input, ChestBoxItemHandler, SpecialItemHandler, and SummonDragon, self-trade and snapshot-overwrite dupes in Trade/TransactionService, an opcode -83 desync in SummonDragonNamek, and unclosed JDBC result sets in Input.

protocol_touchpoints.payload_summary: Sub 0: byte(7), 7*short(icon), byte(typePrice), int(price), short(idTicket); Sub 1: byte(size), size*short(iconID)
byte(0=appear|1=leave); if appear: short(mapId), short(bgId), byte(zoneId), [SummonDragon writes int(pl.id) / SummonDragonNamek OMITS it], UTF, short(x), short(y), byte(type)
0: int(inviterId); 1: int(partnerId); 2: byte(index); 6: int(gold), byte(size), items[short(id), byte/int(qty), opts]; 7: close tab
getItem: byte(type), byte(index); doItem: byte(type 0..4), byte(where), byte(index), optional short(iditem) when index==-1
